[F3] **External input (PL Loop Theorem).** Let $N$ be a triangulated PL $3$-manifold, not necessarily orientable. A continuous map $(D^2,\partial D^2)\to(N,\partial N)$ whose boundary is not null-homotopic in $\partial N$ implies existence of a properly embedded PL disk with essential boundary. We use the PL form in the supplied triangulation, not approximation of the original possibly wild embedding. This is the established Loop Theorem, as stated without orientability in [Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, Theorem3.1, §3.1, printed pp.56–59](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3Mfds.pdf). Its tower starts in the PL category; the proof then presents the disk surgeries smoothly. The theorem is used here as an explicit external input, not as a locally reconstructed PL-category proof.

patches.source_excerpt: 1.1 Apply [F1] to obtain an essential normal disk. The weights of such disks form a nonempty set of positive integers and therefore have a least value. Successively minimize the finitely many normal coordinates among vectors at that weight. Each natural-number minimum leaves a nonempty set, so this finite construction requires no choice principle. [given, F1, construct]
patches.proposed_replacement: 1.1 Regard the supplied essential disk inclusion as a continuous map of pairs and apply [F3]. This gives an essential properly embedded PL disk in the supplied PL manifold; it need not be the original disk or isotopic to it. Apply [F1] to that PL disk to obtain an essential normal disk. The weights of such disks form a nonempty set of positive integers and therefore have a least value. Successively minimize the finitely many normal coordinates among vectors at that weight. Each natural-number minimum leaves a nonempty set, so this finite construction requires no choice principle. [given, F1, F3, construct]
